obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0.1 (service provider)
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; card brand rules
basis: The company stores, processes and transmits account data for card brand members; the three sponsor agreements and the brands' rules require PCI DSS compliance. Level 1 under Visa's service provider levels (more than 300,000 transactions a year); one ROC covers Merchant Acquiring, Integrated Payments and Payouts. No size exemption

obligation: PCI PIN Security Requirements
basis: PIN debit acquiring is validated in a separate PCI PIN assessment and is outside these deliverables

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule
basis: A non-bank financial institution: data processing of financial data is listed in 12 CFR 225.28(b)(14) and is financial in nature under 12 U.S.C. 1843(k) (314.2(h)(1)); it holds customer information of other institutions' customers (314.1(b)). The 314.6 exception does not apply (far more than 5,000 consumers). It has a board, so the Qualified Individual reports to the board (314.4(i)). Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule (bank service provider duty)
applies: Yes, as a bank service provider to Banks A, B and C
basis: Each sponsor agreement names authorization, clearing, settlement, reconciliation and merchant funding file services as performed for the bank and subject to examination under 12 U.S.C. 1867(c), so they are covered services (53.2(b)(5); 304.22(b)(5); 225.301(b)(5)) and the company is a bank service provider to Bank A (53.2(b)(2)), Bank B (304.22(b)(2)) and Bank C (225.301(b)(2)). The banks' own 36-hour notification incident duty (53.3; 225.302; 304.23) does not apply to the company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B; 12 CFR 208 App. D-2; 12 CFR 364 App. B
basis: The Guidelines apply to Banks A, B and C. They reach the company through the sponsor agreements' service provider oversight terms, which the banks test in annual due diligence

obligation: NCUA cyber incident reporting
basis: No group entity is a federally insured credit union, and the company does not sponsor one

obligation: SEC Regulation SCI
basis: No group entity is an SCI entity: no exchange, clearing agency, alternative trading system or plan processor activity

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (Second Amendment)
applies: Yes, for Cris Santos Payouts, LLC
basis: The subsidiary holds a New York money transmitter license, so it is a covered entity (500.1(e)). It is a Class A company (500.1(d)): gross annual revenue of about $210 million in each of the last two fiscal years and about 12,000 employees in the affiliates that share its systems; the 500.19(a) limited exemption is unavailable. It adopted the parent's program under 500.2(d). The parent holds no New York license. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: CIRCIA (pending rule)
basis: Proposed rule only; no final rule at intake. Counsel lists it as an item to watch; reporting to CISA is voluntary until a final rule takes effect

obligation: SEC material cybersecurity incident disclosure
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant and large accelerated filer; no size exemption

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
basis: SEC registrant; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over the ERP and settlement accounting are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Card brand account data compromise rules
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised; American Express DSOP; other brands through the sponsor banks
basis: The company stores, processes and transmits account data for all three sponsor bank programs, and the sponsor agreements require brand compromise procedures and notice to the bank within 24 hours

obligation: Sponsor agreement duties (cutoffs, 24-hour compromise notice, cutoff extension)
citation: Sponsor agreements with Banks A, B and C
basis: Each agreement sets network and bank cutoffs, requires notice of suspected account data compromise within 24 hours, and allows a 2-hour ACH window extension by agreement

obligation: Merchant, ISV partner and SOC report commitments
citation: Merchant and ISV partner agreements; SOC 1 and SOC 2 system descriptions
basis: Merchant agreements promise 99.99% monthly availability for authorization and ISV agreements 99.95% for the Integrated Payments API; SOC 1 and SOC 2 system descriptions set service commitments for user entities

obligation: State breach notification and data security laws
citation: Statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Merchants and cardholders are in all 50 states. For cardholder data the company is usually a third-party agent of its merchants; for merchant owner and workforce data it is the data owner. Counsel's state law matrix was updated in 2026-02

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: Headquartered in Florida with operations in Florida, and holds personal information of Florida residents; third-party agent duty under 501.171(6) for merchants' cardholder data. Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Florida call recording consent (worked example)
basis: The contact centers record merchant calls; Florida requires all-party consent. Relevant to call summarization (AI-006)

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Applies to the company's commerce, including claims about and use of AI in merchant and cardholder decisions

obligation: NYDFS industry letter on AI-related cybersecurity risks
citation: NYDFS industry letter (2024-10-16) under 23 NYCRR Part 500
applies: Yes, as guidance for the payouts subsidiary
basis: Guidance, not a new rule; it explains how a covered entity uses Part 500 to address AI-related risks. AI-001 also scores instant payouts

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (consequential decisions made with AI)
applies: Not determined at intake (counsel review open)
basis: Takes effect 2027-01-01. Whether merchant decisions supported by the models in the AI inventory are covered decisions is a question for counsel; carried to P10

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom or extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the ransom policy requires an OFAC check

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts in the contract repository; recheck if one is signed
